strait-of-hormuz.summary: Effectively closed to normal commercial traffic since 28 Feb: Iran requires permits and fees through its Strait Authority, a US blockade of Iranian ports has been in force since 14 July, and attacks on ships continue — UKMTO logged at least eight vessels struck since 28 Sep, most recently the Aframax tanker On Peace on 5 Oct, which left 12 of its 19 crew injured. Kpler ship-tracking data and satellite imagery showed a 'major operational recovery' at Saudi Arabia's Yanbu terminal, with Hormuz oil flows averaging a 13.2 mb/d 7-day average through 29 Sep (about 77% of Kpler's own ~17 mb/d pre-war baseline). In 29 Sep notes, JPMorgan put regional crude shipments at 17.5 mb/d (98% of pre-war) and Hormuz flows near 13 mb/d, while Goldman Sachs put total Persian Gulf exports, including clandestine shipments, at 23.3 mb/d for September, matching 2025 averages; both banks cautioned this reflects the industry adapting to sustained risk, not improved safety. Tankers still move mainly under naval escort or shuttle arrangements rather than normal free transit, and many sail with transponders off, so independent counts remain partial.

bab-el-mandeb.summary: The Houthis have enforced a 'ban' on Saudi-linked shipping since 20 July, hitting ships (Tihamah 12 Aug, Bahri VLCC off Yanbu 24 Aug) and seizing Mocha and Red Sea islands on 10-11 Sep. Tanker transits fell sharply; overall transits were ~15% below pre-ban levels by late August. Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces launched a counteroffensive ('Operation Yemen Dawn') around 3-5 Oct, backed by a reported 100 Saudi-led coalition jets, and said they had taken full control of the strait plus Dhubab town, its airport and the road to Mokha; Houthi-aligned media denied the advances, and independent confirmation of territorial or shipping-lane control is not yet available, so the status here is unchanged.

east-west-pipeline.summary: Shut 11 Sep after drone strikes on pumping stations (launched from Iraq); restarted around 21-22 Sep and had risen above 80% of its 7 mb/d capacity — close to 6 mb/d, with about 4.5 mb/d available for export after supplying west-coast refineries — by 2 Oct, per a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg. Aramco and the Saudi energy ministry did not comment.

yanbu-terminal.summary: Saudi Arabia's main Hormuz-bypass outlet remains under Houthi missile and drone threat and subject to a declared Houthi ban on Saudi-linked shipping. Throughput has recovered with the East-West pipeline: about 4.5 mb/d was available for export via Yanbu as of 2 Oct after the pipeline topped 80% of capacity, per Bloomberg. France is sending air defences.

kharg-island.summary: The terminal was intact after US strikes on military targets (14 Mar). Iranian exports have been under a US naval blockade since 14 July, and the US struck an Iranian tanker off Kharg on 5 Sep. Tracking group United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), corroborated by Bloomberg vessel-tracking, reported at least 50 Iranian tankers backed up along Iran's coast as of early October, 11 of them laden and anchored east of Kharg with none loading there on 5 Oct; Iran loaded no crude at all in September — the first such month since the war began — with exports falling from about 966,000 b/d in July to roughly 50,000 b/d, as no Iranian crude is known to have crossed the blockade line since 14 July.

ras-tanura-terminal.summary: Loadings are constrained by the Hormuz situation but have partly offset the Yanbu/East-West pipeline outage: Aramco has sold ~60 million barrels of Ras Tanura crude for ship-to-ship transfer at Sohar, Oman this month and next, shipped out via Hormuz by shuttle tanker. Ship-tracking (MarineTraffic, TankerTrackers.com) showed Ras Tanura and Ju'aymah loading ~12–14 mb on 21 Sep, the busiest day since before the war, and the Sohar/Fujairah STS relay is now near capacity.
